prompt:
In many schools a student's final result depends almost entirely on examinations sat at the end of the course. Some people believe that the work a student produces throughout the year should count instead.

To what extent do you agree or disagree?
instruction_line: You should spend about 40 minutes on this task. Write at least 250 words.
key_points: The task expects a clear position: agree / disagree / partly agree
The real comparison is between 'work produced throughout the year' and 'the end-of-term exam' — simply saying exams are stressful is not enough on its own

At least two reasons plus a concrete example: continuous assessment spreads the work over the year and reduces the effect of chance on a single day; an exam, on the other hand, gives a comparable measurement under the same conditions for everyone
A brief concession to the opposing view is expected: coursework throughout the year increases the teacher's workload and can carry inequality in support from home into the final result
The position should be restated clearly at the end
common_mistakes: Listing the good and bad sides of exams without stating a stance
Skipping the question of whether it 'should replace exams' and writing generally about exam anxiety instead
Staying at the level of abstract generalisations without giving examples
